body.title: Impossible to configure_docker, since container_registry_domains is not stored when --use-keyring is supplied and also not checked
body.description:
### Checklist

<!-- Please test the latest versions, that will remove the possibility that you see a bug that is fixed in a newer version. -->

- [x] I'm using the latest version of the extension (Run `glab --version`)
  - Extension version: 1.65.0
- [x] Operating system and version: Fedora 42
- [x] Gitlab.com or self-managed instance? self-managed instance
- [x] GitLab version (if self-managed) 18.05
- [x] I have performed `glab auth status` to check for authentication issues
- [ ] Run the command in debug mode (like `DEBUG=true glab mr list`) and attach any useful output

### Summary

Using `glab auth login` with `--use-keyring` does not store the survey answer to supplied container registry domains.

Additionally `glab auth status` does not check for validity of container registry credentials.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Login with `glab auth login --use-keyring` and provide container registry domains
2. Try to do `glab auth configure-docker`
3. See the error

### What is the current _bug_ behavior?

The error is thrown:

```
ERROR: no hosts were configured - ensure you've logged in via oauth2 and configured at least one container registry domain for a host
```

### What is the expected _correct_ behavior?

`configure_docker` succeeds and container registry domains are retained when using the keyring, as without using `--use-keyring`.

Else the error could also be more understandable, such as "no container registries found in configuration retrieved from keyring/configuration file at path …".

body.title: Remove the experimental `glab mcp serve` command in favour of the GitLab MCP Server
body.description:
## Summary

As [requested in !3093](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/cli/-/merge_requests/3093#note_3944378084), deprecate, then remove, the experimental `glab mcp` command and its supporting code, and direct users to the [GitLab MCP Server](https://docs.gitlab.com/user/model_context_protocol/mcp_server/).

## Why

- **Two GitLab MCP servers confuse users.** Users compare the two and report tool counts from one against the other ([gitlab#588956](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab/-/work_items/588956)). The GitLab MCP Server is the documented, supported path.
- **The original reason to use `glab mcp serve` is gone.** It was used to work around the GitLab MCP Server being Premium/Ultimate only. The GitLab MCP Server is now available on Free, Premium, and Ultimate, across GitLab.com, Self-Managed, and Dedicated ([gitlab-org&21183](https://gitlab.com/groups/gitlab-org/-/work_items/21183)), and is working towards GA ([gitlab-org&19117](https://gitlab.com/groups/gitlab-org/-/work_items/19117)).
- **It was always meant to be temporary.** The original MR planned to "swap this one out with the official server when it's ready" ([!2361](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/cli/-/merge_requests/2361)).
- **Agents with a shell don't need it.** Coding agents can run `glab` directly, using `--help` and `--output json`. The MCP wrapper re-exposes the same commands at a large context cost.
- **It has a maintenance cost.** Every command carries MCP annotations (`internal/mcpannotations`, referenced from ~230 files), and the server has its own schema generation, flag handling, response capping, and an MCP SDK dependency.

The feature is marked experimental, so it can be removed under the [experiment support policy](https://docs.gitlab.com/policy/development_stages_support/).

Usage metrics for `glab mcp serve` and per-tool MCP calls are posted in an internal comment on this issue.

## Proposal

**Timing:** deprecate when the GitLab MCP Server reaches GA ([gitlab-org&19117](https://gitlab.com/groups/gitlab-org/-/work_items/19117)), then remove one milestone later.

1. **Deprecate, in the milestone the GitLab MCP Server reaches GA.** Set cobra's `Deprecated` on `glab mcp` and `glab mcp serve`, following the [deprecation message conventions](https://docs.gitlab.com/development/documentation/cli_styleguide/#deprecation-messages). The message says the command is scheduled to be removed and points to the GitLab MCP Server docs. `make gen-docs` removes the command's pages. Implemented in [!3998](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/cli/-/merge_requests/3998), to merge once the GitLab MCP Server is GA.
2. **Remove, one milestone after deprecation.** Delete `internal/commands/mcp/`, the `invocation_source` telemetry property, and the `github.com/modelcontextprotocol/go-sdk` dependency. The command annotations stay, because read-only mode ([#8353](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/cli/-/work_items/8353)) will reuse the read/write classification. Implemented in [!4014](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/cli/-/merge_requests/4014).

[!3093](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/cli/-/merge_requests/3093) is a proof of concept for step 2 and can be used as a starting point.

## Open questions

- **Local-only commands (answered from usage data).** Earlier discussion ([!2361](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/cli/-/merge_requests/2361)) suggested keeping a slimmed `glab mcp` for commands that only make sense locally, such as `glab cluster agent update-kubeconfig` and `glab opentofu init`. Usage data (see the internal comment) shows none of these commands were called through MCP. Agents that use them run `glab` from the shell instead, so we don't plan to keep a slimmed `glab mcp`.
- **Rate limits.** The GitLab MCP Server [limits requests](https://docs.gitlab.com/user/model_context_protocol/mcp_server/) to 60 per minute on Free and 600 per minute per user on Premium and Ultimate. `glab mcp serve` falls under the standard API rate limits. Will heavy agent workloads, especially on Free, hit the GitLab MCP Server limits?
- **Governance controls (answered).** `glab mcp serve` has no user-configurable controls. Tool exposure is fixed in code, and write tools only carry a `destructiveHint` for the client. The GitLab MCP Server already offers more: an instance or top-level group setting to allow access, per-client toolset selection, an `mcp` OAuth scope, and read/write tool annotations. Removing `glab mcp serve` doesn't take away any governance control.
- **Release mechanics. (answered)** Removing an experimental command does not require a breaking-change. So the automated release will work as per normal.

## Related issues to close or update

- [#8147](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/cli/-/work_items/8147): serve Agent Skills via the MCP subcommand.
- [#8058](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/cli/-/work_items/8058): filter tools on the MCP server.

## Related

- [gitlab#588956](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab/-/work_items/588956): GitLab MCP server vs Glab MCP server.
- [gitlab-org&19117](https://gitlab.com/groups/gitlab-org/-/work_items/19117): GitLab MCP Server GA.
- [!3093](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/cli/-/merge_requests/3093): draft removal PoC.

body.title: glab repo clone using a full URL authenticates to gitlab.com
body.description:
### Checklist

<!-- Please test the latest versions, that will remove the possibility that you see a bug that is fixed in a newer version. -->

- [X] I'm using the latest version of the extension (Run `glab --version`)
- [X] Gitlab.com or self-managed instance? _both_
- [X] I have performed `glab auth status` to check for authentication issues

### Summary

<!-- Summarize the bug encountered concisely -->

### Steps to reproduce

Set an incorrect/empty token for the gitlab.com host entry in `~/.config/glab-cli/config.yml`
Set `host` to gitlab.com in `~/.config/glab-cli/config.yml` or remove `host` as it will default to gitlab.com


`glab repo clone https://mygitlab.com/mygroup/myrepo`

<!-- How one can reproduce the issue - this is very important -->

### What is the current _bug_ behavior?
`GET https://gitlab.com/api/v4/user: 401 {message: 401 Unauthorized}`
<!-- What actually happens -->

### What is the expected _correct_ behavior?
repo is cloned similar to:

`GITLAB_HOST=mygitlab.com glab repo clone https://mygitlab.com/mygroup/myrepo`
<!-- What you should see instead -->

### Workaround

Set `host` to your desired env in `~/.config/glab-cli/config.yml`

<!-- If you can, link to the line of code that might be responsible for the problem -->
